static_traits.name: Li Ming
static_traits.social_status: The relationship with the spouse is affected by avoiding driving-related activities; tends to avoid social activities involving driving or transport; the spouse is generally supportive but the client finds it hard to communicate deeply on this specific problem
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problem history yet; never received psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Neutral attitude, clear logical thinking, able to self-reflect and identify cognitive biases; expressing self-labeling and catastrophizing tendencies (such as 'failure', 'terrible athlete'); fairly high cooperation; prone to self-blame and perfectionistic demands under pressure, and less patient with family after emotional setbacks

basic_info.main_problem: Because I cannot drive, I see myself as a 'failure', triggering low self-esteem and worthlessness, and leading to avoidance of driving- and traffic-related social activities.
basic_info.core_demands: The impact of this belief on my self-esteem and daily life made me realize I need professional help and support.
growth_experiences: Starting in late adolescence, due to society's expectations and pressure around driving, I linked 'not being able to drive' with 'failure / not being recognized'; this belief has become more prominent in recent years. I tried taking driving lessons, but fear and anxiety were too strong to persist.

A few months ago, missing a run due to bad weather triggered intense self-criticism and labeling (e.g. 'I am a terrible athlete'); since then, whenever plans are disrupted (e.g. running, cooking not going well), I tend to generalize local mistakes into 'I fail at everything', and have become more irritable with family, with decreased patience.

core_beliefs: As long as I cannot persist as planned, I am just a failure (conditional self-worth)

special_situations.event: Sees others driving or driving topics come up in conversation
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot drive, it shows I am unqualified and will be dismissed by society and others
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding social situations involving driving and traffic; trying to enroll in driving lessons but withdrawing due to overwhelming anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot drive, so I am a failure / inferior to others

special_situations.event: Missing a run due to bad weather, causing the training plan to not be completed on time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot strictly follow the plan, it equals total failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Next time push oneself harder to 'make up for' the mistake
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Not persisting means I am a failure; I fail at everything

special_situations.event: Small mistakes in housework (e.g. cooking), results not meeting expectations
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Any flaw at all proves I cannot do anything well
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Strengthens self-criticism, raises perfection standards and sense of control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just terrible at everything / cannot do it

special_situations.event: Even when things go smoothly, worries the next challenge will go wrong
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Good results are just luck; next time it will very likely fail again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Persistent tension, pressures herself in advance to avoid 'failing again'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Next time something will very likely go wrong again / it is hard for me to maintain a good state

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized, to be seen as capable and worthy
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged and dismissed by others, worrying about being seen as a failure and feeling ashamed
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being judged and maintaining a sense of control by avoiding driving-related situations and self-reproach

object_relations.self_representation: Unqualified, a self prone to failure
A self who tries hard but is misunderstood

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites her to view the 'failure' label from a more balanced perspective or proposes concrete practice steps
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Feels their real plight may be simplified, worried they will again have to 'meet the standard' and be judged
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Affirming their logical ability in a gentle, empathetic tone, while inviting them to attend to present emotions and bodily sensations; reducing the density of rational persuasion, using open-ended questioning and concretizing exercises, helping them name shame and anxiety in a safe atmosphere.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing details of a missed run or a housework mistake
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizing unfavorable external factors as full self-attribution, believing all problems are with me
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Reducing judgmental language, using affirmation and normalization strategies; through dialogue distinguishing controllable from uncontrollable factors, guiding them to externalize unreasonable full self-attribution and practice a fairer self-narrative.

manifestations: Linking 'not being able to drive' with 'I am a failure / unworthy', feeling self-worth depends on meeting social expectations (whether I can drive)
outcomes: Avoiding socializing and activities leading to a narrowed life scope

manifestations: Feeling bound by social rules (everyone should be able to drive), finding it hard to define value by one's own standards
outcomes: Reduced decision-making and life freedom (unwilling to participate in driving-related activities)

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Viewing partial mistakes as overall failure and judging oneself harshly

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves.
manifestations: After missing a run, turning stress and aggression toward oneself, forcing oneself to try harder next time
Handles mistakes caused by external factors (such as weather) more through self-blame

positive_force: Has effective household management ability (competent in daily family duties)
Has a supportive spouse to confide in
Willing to seek professional help and take part in structured practice
Able to identify and discuss own cognitive biases (logically seeing the unreasonableness)
Once actively tried to change the status quo through driving lessons
negative_force: Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking are prominent
Fear and anxiety about driving leading to avoidance
Strong internalization of social expectations, relying on external evaluation to define self-worth
Self-blame and stress make one more irritable toward family and less patient

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids social activities and daily affairs related to driving and traffic
antecedent: Needs to take part in activities requiring driving/transport arrangements
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizing social expectations as personal value judgments (not being able to drive = failure), accompanied by catastrophic worry about being judged and shame
target_behavior.function: Avoiding situations of being judged and shame, lowering anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Restricted errands and social participation, narrowed life scope, relationship with spouse affected

target_behavior.behavior: Self-reproach and negative labeling when plans are disrupted (e.g. missing a run or cooking not going well immediately means 'I fail at everything')
antecedent: Housework or cooking results not meeting expectations
target_behavior.core_reason: Conditional self-worth and perfectionist standards (counting as valuable only if plan targets are met), accompanied by all-or-nothing and overgeneralization cognitive biases
target_behavior.function: Tries to maintain a sense of control and prevent failing again through self-pressure
target_behavior.consequence: Worsened sense of frustration and anxiety, more irritable with family and less patient, overall impaired self-esteem
